description: Synthetic but user-shaped pilot set for validating graded RAG labels before collecting a real 100-300 query corpus.

fixtures.content:
# Current audit retention policy
Policy code AURORA_RETENTION_47X is effective from 2026-01-01. Security audit records are retained for 47 months. This policy is authoritative and supersedes all earlier retention notes.
fixtures.padding: Operational examples explain how ordinary audit records are classified and exported. These examples do not change the retention duration.
fixtures.tail:
## Legal hold exception
A legal hold pauses scheduled deletion even after the normal 47-month period. Records remain held until Legal releases the hold.

fixtures.content:
# Archived retention policy
RETIRED in 2025. This historical document required audit records to be kept for 36 months. Do not use it for current decisions.

# Customer refund policy
Current policy: customers may request a refund within seven days after order completion. Support verifies the order owner before approving the request.

# Archived refund policy
RETIRED: an older promotion allowed refund requests for fourteen days. It ended in 2025 and is not current policy.

# Refund event logging
After an approved refund enters the payment service, engineers attach an internal trace identifier to refund event delivery logs. This is an observability procedure, not the customer eligibility policy.

# Service disaster recovery
The primary application has a recovery time objective of 30 minutes. Traffic fails over to the secondary region using cross-region replicas.

# Database disaster recovery
The production database has a recovery time objective of 45 minutes. Recovery restores encrypted snapshots and replays the transaction log.

# SSO onboarding
An administrator first assigns the employee to the AuroraDesk SSO application. On first login, the employee enrolls MFA and stores recovery codes.

# SSO outage troubleshooting
During an SSO outage, operators verify identity-provider metadata, certificate expiry and clock skew. This runbook is not the user setup guide.

# Account recovery
A user who forgot a password selects Forgot password and receives an email recovery link. The link expires after 20 minutes. SSO users should use their identity-provider recovery flow.

# Webhook delivery
Webhook requests include the X-Aurora-Signature header. Receivers verify the body with HMAC-SHA256 before accepting the event. Failed deliveries enter the retry queue.

# Integration retry schedule
Failed webhook deliveries retry after 1 minute, 5 minutes and 30 minutes. A delivery that still fails is placed in the dead-letter queue.

# Billing invoices
Workspace owners download a tax invoice from Billing, then Invoices. The legal name and billing address can be corrected before the monthly invoice closes.

# Invoice API object
For developers, the invoice JSON object contains id, currency, subtotal and status fields. This reference does not explain how a customer downloads a tax invoice.

# Subscription cancellation
A workspace owner opens Billing, chooses Manage plan and selects Cancel subscription. Access remains active until the end of the paid billing cycle.

# Mobile offline mode
The mobile app can read previously synchronized tickets without a network connection. Editing and sending replies require reconnecting; queued drafts sync when the app is online.

# Public API rate limits
The standard workspace limit is 120 requests per minute per access token. A 429 response includes the Retry-After header.

# Backup operations
The daily encrypted backup begins at 02:10 UTC. Backups are replicated to the paired recovery region and verified before rotation.

# Data residency
European customer data is stored in the eu-west primary region. Disaster-recovery copies remain inside the paired EU recovery region.

# Account data deletion
After an owner confirms workspace deletion, active customer data is removed within 30 days. Encrypted backup copies expire under the separate backup lifecycle.

# Cache cleanup job
A maintenance worker removes expired application cache entries every hour. Cache cleanup does not delete customer accounts or authoritative records.

# Workspace data export
Owners request an export from Settings, Data controls. The job produces a signed download link.
fixtures.padding: The export guide lists progress states, notification behavior and examples for ordinary workspace records.
fixtures.tail:
## Delivery limits
An export is prepared within 24 hours. Each downloadable archive is limited to 2 GB; larger exports are split into numbered archives.

fixtures.content:
# Current Enterprise SLA
Effective 2026, the Enterprise plan monthly uptime commitment is 99.95 percent. This document supersedes the archived SLA.
fixtures.padding: Availability measurements exclude customer-controlled networks and announced maintenance windows. Monthly reports show eligible service minutes.
fixtures.tail:
## Service credits
When measured uptime falls below 99.95 percent, the workspace owner must submit a service-credit request within 30 days of the incident report.

fixtures.content:
# Archived Enterprise SLA
RETIRED in 2025. The former monthly uptime commitment was 99.9 percent. It must not be used for current credit decisions.

# Incident response handbook
This handbook describes ownership, communication channels and severity review.
fixtures.padding: Responders record observations, preserve timestamps and keep the incident channel focused on verified operational facts.
fixtures.tail:
## Severity two acknowledgement
Code ORBIT_SEV2 requires the on-call incident commander to acknowledge the page within 15 minutes.

fixtures.content:
# Python SDK guide
The client supports retries, pagination and idempotency keys for write requests.
fixtures.padding: Examples demonstrate typed request objects, response inspection and safe retry behavior for ordinary API operations.
fixtures.tail:
## Timeout
The Python SDK default request timeout is 30 seconds. Callers may override it per client or per request.
